purpose: Cross-implementation agreement on the canonical tool-call action material. The material is {"tool":<name>,"args":<arguments>} canonicalized per JCS (RFC 8785). Every EMILIA framework adapter, in every language, MUST produce byte-identical action digests for these inputs.
excluded: A semantic selector or routing hint is NOT material: it is derived from arguments already inside the digest.
why_this_exists: Two shipped adapters diverged. The TypeScript binder in packages/require-receipt hashed the member as "args"; the CrewAI Python adapter hashed it as "arguments" and additionally hashed an optional selector the TypeScript binder excludes. The same logical call produced two different action digests, so a receipt minted through one adapter could never verify against the other. No test caught it because no conformance suite covered a framework adapter. Nothing in CAID, AEB or the receipts draft fixed the member name, so neither implementation was wrong: the specification was silent.
